title: Grauert–Remmert finiteness over an algebraically closed analytic field
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field with a nontrivial rank-one absolute value and valuation ring $V=\{x:|x|\leq1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Let $C$ be a reduced affinoid $K$-algebra, meaning a reduced quotient of a Tate algebra $K\langle T_1,\ldots,T_n\rangle$ of restricted power series. Write $C^\circ$ for the elements $c$ for which the set $\{c^m:m\geq0\}$ is bounded in the affinoid Banach topology. Let $D\subseteq C^\circ$ be a $V$-subalgebra which, with its induced topology, is a quotient of $V\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle$ and whose natural map $D\otimes_VK\to C$ is an isomorphism. Then $C^\circ$ is a finite $D$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. The zero affinoid algebra is allowed.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, Step 2, printed p. 22; BGR §6.4 and 6.4.1/4 as cited there; primary PDF read online, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: If $C=0$, then $C^\circ=0$ is generated by the empty set, so assume $C\ne0$. Choose $\pi\in V$ with $0<|\pi|<1$. Then $K=V[1/\pi]$: multiplying any scalar by a sufficiently large power of $\pi$ puts it in $V$. The same argument applies to a restricted series, since its coefficients are bounded, so $K\langle T\rangle=V\langle T\rangle[1/\pi]$. Localize the given surjection $V\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle\to D$ and use $D\otimes_V K\cong C$. This gives a surjection $q_0:K\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle\to C$ whose unit-ball image is $D$. It is continuous: on the open unit ball it is the given continuous map into $D$ followed by the inclusion into $C$, and elsewhere continuity follows by scalar multiplication.

u\in V$ tending to zero. This is evaluation of a restricted series in the distinguished presentation; the sum converges in $C$.

source.place: BGR Theorem 6.4.3/1 and 6.4.3/6, as confirmed in Rodriguez Vazquez, section 2.2, p. 1685 (preceding Proposition 2.2).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affinoid-powerbounded-integral] to $q_0$ from step 1 and each $b_i$ from step 2. Thus there are integers $d_i\geq1$ and elements $h_{ij}\in D$ with $b_i^{d_i}=-\sum_{0\leq j<d_i}h_{ij}b_i^j$. The coefficient ring here is precisely $D=q_0(V\langle T\rangle)$, not the unit ball from the new distinguished presentation. This is the only integrality input.

source.place: Bosch section 1.4, Theorem 16 and Proposition 4(iii), pp. 28-29 and 23.

u\alpha})b^\alpha$, with the inner sum taken over that finite partial set. Passing to the limit gives $c=\sum_{\alpha\in E}\lambda_\alpha b^\alpha$. Indeed the map from the $\pi$-adically topologized $D$ to $C$ is continuous, since it is induced by the given topological quotient $V\langle Tangle	o D\subset C$; finite sums and multiplication by each $b^\alpha$ preserve limits. Thus the finite family $(b^\alpha)_{\alpha\in E}$ generates $C^\circ$ over $D$, which is exactly [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. If $s=0$, $E$ consists of the single empty monomial $1$, and the same argument applies.
